quizzes.stem: A synthesis subagent often needs to confirm a date or a name while it writes. Each time it returns control to the coordinator, which calls the search subagent and then the synthesis subagent again, and latency has grown by about 40 percent. Most checks are simple lookups and a few need real investigation. What is the best design?

options.a: Give it a small verifier tool for the quick cases and route the hard ones through the hub
options.b: Let the synthesis subagent collect every check and return them in one batch at the end
options.c: Give the synthesis subagent each of the search tools so that it can answer any check itself
options.d: Have the search subagent save extra context around each source in case a check comes up

explanation.a: A narrow tool serves the frequent case and the coordinator keeps the rare one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Waiting to hand back all the checks at the end blocks later steps that depend on earlier verified facts".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Giving the synthesis agent every search tool over-provisions it and brings back the misuse".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Speculative caching cannot reliably predict what the synthesis agent will need to check".

quizzes.stem: An analysis subagent holds a general `fetch_url` tool, and it sometimes fetches pages that have nothing to do with the documents it was given. Which change fits best?

options.a: Add a sentence to its prompt saying that only links to the supplied files may be fetched
options.b: Swap it for a loader that takes only the job's links and refuses the rest with a reason
options.c: Take the tool away and have the coordinator paste each file's text into the brief by hand
options.d: Give it a second tool that reports the host of each link before the fetch is made

explanation.b: A constraint inside the tool holds whatever the model decides.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an instruction not to use a tool is a request, and a tool the agent holds is a tool it can use".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Taking a tool away is not the fix when the role really needs the capability".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "adding a tool to describe the first adds to the list and restricts nothing".

quizzes.stem: To force a first tool on a model that rejects forcing, a team offers only that tool in the first request and the full list in every later one. Which cost does the first change carry?

options.a: Only the message blocks are processed again, as for any change of tool choice
options.b: Nothing is processed again, since definitions that are removed stay cached
options.c: Only the system prompt is processed again, because it sits above the messages
options.d: The whole cached prefix is processed again, since the definitions differ

explanation.d: Changing the definitions changes the first layer of the cache, and every layer after it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because that holds only for the choice: "Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache".
explanation.b: is ruled out for the same reason, since the list is part of the cached prefix: "Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the layers cascade downward: "Changes at each level invalidate that level and all subsequent levels."

quizzes.stem: In this module's example, a loop on Claude Sonnet 5.5 offers the one required tool with `auto`, and a reply comes back as plain text with no tool call. What should the loop do?

options.a: Accept the text as the answer and go on to the next step
options.b: Resend the request with `any` as the choice and expect a call
options.c: Count it as a miss and ask once more before escalating
options.d: Repeat the same request until the turn limit ends the run

explanation.c: With `auto` the table's guarantee is "Nothing: it may answer in text", so a missed call is a miss that the loop handles.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A reply of text only, when a call was required, is a miss".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the parameter is refused there: "`any` and `tool` return a 400 error".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Looping until the turn limit turns a missed call into a run that ends with nothing".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. The tool that closes a customer's account carries a description that asks the model to use it with care. What should restrict it?

options.a: A longer note in its description, with an example of when not to call it
options.b: A required parameter in which the model states its reason for each call
options.c: A system prompt rule that forbids the call unless the customer asks for it
options.d: A server-side check of ownership and a human approval before it runs

explanation.d: Closing an account cannot be undone, so the tool layer compares the call with the verified customer and holds it for an approval, which no wording from the model can get around.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A note in the tool's description that asks for care is an instruction".
explanation.b: Ruled out because a field in which the model states its reason "is a claim by the model, not a check".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a prompt rule is still "an instruction not to use a tool", and "an instruction not to use a tool is a request".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S1, a customer support resolution agent. The agent handles returns, billing disputes and account problems with tools that verify identity, look up orders and issue refunds, and it escalates to a person when it cannot resolve a case. Refunds cannot be undone, and this module's tool layer caps them at 500. A call for 450 arrives and nobody has approved it. What should the tool layer return?

options.a: A result that runs the refund and logs that the amount is under the cap
options.b: A result that runs the refund and notifies a person to review it afterwards
options.c: A flagged refusal that stays on hold until a human signs off on this one
options.d: A flagged refusal that sends the case to a person who can raise the cap

explanation.c: A refund cannot be undone, so it waits for a person's approval even under the cap.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "An irreversible call needs an approval even when the amount is under the cap".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "a review after the fact cannot undo an irreversible call".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the route to a person who can raise the limit is for an amount above the cap: "An amount above the cap is refused and sent to a person", and 450 is under 500.

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator delegates to a web search subagent, a document analysis subagent and a synthesis subagent, and it produces a cited report. All subagents hold the same 18 tools, including the one that sends the finished report, and the synthesis subagent has begun running web searches. Which redesign fits best?

options.a: Split the list by role, and give the irreversible step one owner and an approval
options.b: Keep one list, and add a prompt line for each role naming the tools it may use
options.c: Cut the shared list to the ten most used tools, and give it to every role alike
options.d: Keep the 18 tools, and route each request through a classifier that picks a subset

explanation.a: Scoped lists remove the misuse, and the irreversible step has an owner and an approval.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a prompt line is a request: "an instruction not to use a tool is a request, and a tool the agent holds is a tool it can use".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "an agent outside its specialisation misuses what it holds".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a router adds a component to keep correct".
